Subject: Post-call recap: ACME performance SLOs & concurrency ask

Hi Kate / Tom —

Thanks for the call today — good to walk through ACME's expected traffic shape. Recap + next steps below so we're aligned: 

Summary of requirements you gave us:
- Streaming chat experience for customer support assistant (server -> client streaming).
- Typical response length: ~200–300 tokens; 95th percentile request size ~512 tokens for edge cases.
- Target SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency <= 600ms for interactive flows (streaming enabled), avg latency target ~300–400ms for 256‑token responses.
- Traffic shape:
  - Sustained throughput: ~200 requests/sec (across multiple regions).
  - Peak burst: up to 500 requests/sec for short windows (1–3 minutes).
  - Concurrent streaming connections: avg ~40, peak ~150 simultaneous open streams.
  - Avg tokens per minute estimate (pilot): ~250k–350k tokens/minute at peak.

Questions / things we agreed I'll follow up on:
1) How Redwood counts concurrency for streaming connections vs short-lived requests (we'll confirm semantics below).
2) Recommended client-side connection strategy (pooling/keep-alive, SSE vs chunked responses).
3) Proposal for a pilot quota (baseline concurrency + burst) and associated pilot pricing/credits.
4) SE-run load test cadence and timeframe.

Proposed next steps: 
- I'll share a draft pilot quote today that includes a dedicated concurrency/burst profile and a short pilot credit. (Attached: ACME_pilot_quote_v1.pdf)
- Can we schedule a 60‑minute session with one of our SEs next week to run a controlled streaming load test? I can propose Wed/Thu.
- Please confirm whether the token estimates above match your internal forecast so we can size the pilot.

Thanks — appreciate the thoroughness on the call.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap, that looks right from our end. A few clarifying items before we lock the pilot: 

1) Concurrency semantics: when you say "concurrent streaming connections" does Redwood count a streaming SSE/HTTP2 connection as occupying a concurrency slot for its full lifetime (i.e., while the stream is open), or do you have a separate per-connection quota? We have long‑lived customer sessions that stay open for several minutes.

2) Rate limits vs queuing: if we hit the baseline but are within a short burst window, will requests be queued for a short time, or will clients get 429s immediately? We want graceful degradation for chat UX.

3) Client behavior: we plan to run multiple backend servers sharing the same API key. Any recommendations for connection pooling or per-instance limits (HTTP keep‑alive settings, connection reuse)?

4) Pilot timing: Targeting a 2‑week pilot in Q2. Can SE run a streaming load test that exercises 150 concurrent streams and a 500 RPS burst?

If you can confirm the above and share the pilot quote + SE times, we'll finalize internally.

Thanks,

Thanks Kate — great questions, answers below and a proposed pilot profile.

1) Concurrency semantics: Redwood counts "concurrency" as active in‑flight requests for the account/API key. For streaming (SSE/HTTP chunked), the connection holds the concurrency slot for the full duration of the open stream. In other words, a long‑lived stream = one concurrency unit while open.

2) Rate limits vs queuing: Default hosted behavior is to return a 429 once you exceed your configured concurrency or rate limit. For Dedicated and larger customers we offer a configurable queue policy (short in‑memory queue) so transient bursts can be buffered instead of dropping immediately. For the pilot I recommend enabling a short queue window (up to 15s) so UX remains smooth for momentary spikes.

3) Client recommendations: 
- Use persistent HTTP connections (keep‑alive) and connection reuse; avoid new TCP/TLS handshakes per request.
- For streaming we recommend HTTP/1.1 with chunked responses or HTTP/2 for multiplexed streams; SSE is fine for browser clients.
- Use a shared API key per logical customer tenant (so limits are applied at the account level) and do client‑side exponential backoff for 429s.

4) Pilot profile & proposal (proposed in attached quote):
- Baseline concurrency: 150 concurrent slots
- Burst capacity: up to 500 concurrent slots for short windows (<= 3 minutes)
- Token budget during pilot: 10M tokens total over 2 weeks (we can adjust based on your forecast)
- Queue policy: short queue (10–15s) enabled
- SE load test: Redwood SE can schedule a 90‑minute streaming load test next week — proposed slots Wed 11am or Thu 2pm PT.

Notes on implementation: the concurrency slots are applied at the account level (per-organization), so you can share one API key across backend instances. We will monitor 429 rates and latency during the SE run.

If that aligns, I'll mark the pilot quote as final and include it in the deal record (ACME-2026-042).

Best,
Marissa
